intro_en: You will learn to say how many people are in your family and to talk about brothers, sisters, and children. You will also see how English adds -s to make plurals, while Mongolian uses the bare noun after a number.
intro_mn: Та гэр бүлдээ хэдэн хүн байгааг, ах дүү, хүүхдүүдийнхээ тухай хэлж сурна. Мөн англи хэлэнд олон тоог -s-ээр хэрхэн хийдгийг, монгол хэлэнд тооны дараа үгийг хэвээр нь хэрэглэдгийг үзнэ.

vocab.example_en: There are five people in our family.
My older brother lives in Ulaanbaatar.
My younger sibling goes to school.
How many younger siblings do you have?
There are six people in total.

sentences.mn: Танай гэр бүлд хэдэн хүн бий вэ?
sentences.en: How many people are in your family?
alt_mn: Танай гэр бүлд хэдэн хүн байдаг вэ?
alt_en: How many people are there in your family?
sentences.mn_latin: Tanai ger büld kheden khün bii ve?

sentences.mn: Манай гэр бүлд таван хүн бий.
sentences.en: There are five people in my family.
sentences.mn_latin: Manai ger büld tavan khün bii.

sentences.en: How many older sisters do you have?
alt_en: How many sisters do you have?

sentences.en: My younger siblings go to school.
alt_en: My younger brothers and sisters go to school.

alt_en: There are six of us in total.

alt_en: The teachers are seated at the table.
sentences.mn_latin: Bagsh nar shireenii ard suuj baina.

sentences.en: I don't have a younger sibling.

grammar.explain_en: In Mongolian, after a number or хэдэн ('how many'), the noun stays in its basic form: хоёр ах (two older brothers), гурван хүүхэд (three children). Do not add a plural ending. When there is no number, нар (written as a separate word) shows several people, for example багш нар (teachers), ах нар (older brothers). Other words take plural endings such as -ууд/-үүд or -чууд: хүүхдүүд (children). Note: гурав becomes гурван before a noun.
grammar.explain_mn: Англи хэлэнд нэр үгийн олон тоог ихэвчлэн -s залгаж үүсгэнэ: brother → brothers, sister → sisters. Монгол хэлэнд "хоёр ах" гэж тооны дараа олон тооны нөхцөл хэрэглэдэггүй ч англиар тооны дараа заавал олон тоо хэрэглэнэ: two brothers. Зарим үг энгийн бус олон тоотой: child → children, person → people, man → men, woman → women. Нэг гэвэл ганц тоо: one brother.

dialogue.speaker: Bat
dialogue.mn: Сайн байна уу, Эмили! Манайд тавтай морил.
dialogue.en: Hello, Emily! Welcome to our home.
dialogue.mn_latin: Sain baina uu, Emili! Manaid tavtai moril.

dialogue.speaker: Emily
dialogue.mn: Баярлалаа, Бат. Танай гэр бүлд хэдэн хүн бий вэ?
dialogue.en: Thank you, Bat. How many people are in your family?
dialogue.mn_latin: Bayarlalaa, Bat. Tanai ger büld kheden khün bii ve?

dialogue.speaker: Bat
dialogue.mn: Нийт зургаан хүн бий: аав, ээж, хоёр эгч, би, дүү.
dialogue.en: Six people in total: Dad, Mom, two older sisters, me, and my younger sibling.
dialogue.mn_latin: Niit zurgaan khün bii: aav, eej, khoyor egch, bi, düü.

dialogue.speaker: Bat
dialogue.mn: Тэд гал тогоонд буузаа хийж байна.
dialogue.en: They are making buuz in the kitchen.
dialogue.mn_latin: Ted gal togoond buuzaa khiij baina.

dialogue.speaker: Emily
dialogue.mn: Манай гэр бүлд дөрвөн хүн бий. Надад нэг ах бий.
dialogue.en: There are four people in my family. I have one older brother.
dialogue.mn_latin: Manai ger büld dörvön khün bii. Nadad neg akh bii.

dialogue.speaker: Bat
dialogue.mn: Манай гэр бүл танайхаас том юм байна.
dialogue.en: My family is bigger than yours.
dialogue.mn_latin: Manai ger bül tanaikhaas tom yum baina.

dialogue.speaker: Emily
dialogue.mn: Тийм ээ, гэхдээ танай бууз үнэхээр амттай байна!
dialogue.en: Yes, but your buuz is really delicious!
dialogue.mn_latin: Tiim ee, gekhdee tanai buuz ünekheer amttai baina!

culture_note.en: In Mongolia, families often gather for a big dinner, especially on weekends and at Tsagaan Sar, and several generations may live together in one home or ger. Making buuz together is a favorite family activity. Mongolian has special words for older and younger siblings (ах, эгч, дүү), so people say which one they mean.
culture_note.mn: Монголд гэр бүлийнхэн амралтын өдрүүдэд, ялангуяа Цагаан сараар нэг ширээний ард цуглаж хамтдаа хоол иддэг. Хэд хэдэн үе нэг гэр, байшинд хамт амьдрах нь элбэг. Бууз хамт хийх нь гэр бүлийн дуртай ажил. Монгол хэлэнд ах, эгч, дүү гэсэн тусдаа үгс байдаг тул хэнийг хэлж байгаагаа нарийн хэлдэг.

review.notes: Mostly good; main errors are an ungrammatical English alt, gender added to дүү in dialogue, and a weak distractor (тэй).

opus_fix.notes: Mainly fixed plural spelling with нар, non-unique fill-blank options, and the grammar and culture mismatches.

changes.why: Misspelling: нар is written as a separate word (дүү нар).
'гэр бүл их' is not natural; олуулаа is the usual word for a big family.
'хүүхэд нар' is colloquial; хүүхдүүд is the standard plural.
нар is a separate word, and -ууд/-д are not mainly for people.
Distractors were misspelled or non-existent forms.
'persons' is also grammatical, so the answer was not the only correct option.
The suffix -ы on an English word is wrong.
Манай is the natural choice with гэр бүл.
Now matches the English: weekends and Tsagaan Sar, and favorite family activity.
